title: Commission takes action to ensure complete and timely transposition of EU directives: key decisions on energy
date_evidence: 25 September 2026 (date line of the DG Energy news item)
key_claim: Letters of formal notice went to 26 Member States on the recast Hydrogen and Decarbonised Gas Directive (deadline 5 August 2026), where only Italy had notified full transposition, and to 18 on the electricity market design Directive 2024/1711 (deadline 17 July 2026).
frame_summary: The Commission presents late transposition as a routine enforcement step and gives each recipient two months to respond before a reasoned opinion.
verbatim_quote: To date, only Italy has notified full transposition of the Directive by the legal deadline.
verbatim_list: To date, 18 EU countries have not yet notified full transposition of these provisions by the legal deadline.
EU countries had to notify the transposition of the Directive to transpose the rules into national law by 5 August 2026.
If they fail to do so, the Commission may pass to a next step and issue a reasoned opinion.
notes: WebFetch 19/10/2026 verbatim extraction. Counts of 26 and 18 recipients come from the country lists on the page.

title: October infringements package: key decisions on energy
date_evidence: 1 October 2026 (date line of the DG Energy news item)
key_claim: On the recast Energy Efficiency Directive the Commission sent reasoned opinions to Greece, Spain, Italy and Malta after letters of formal notice to 26 Member States in November 2025; it referred Bulgaria to the Court of Justice on the Electricity Directive, whose deadline was 31 December 2020.
frame_summary: The Commission shows that transposition cases escalate slowly, with the oldest reaching court nearly six years after the deadline.
verbatim_quote: The deadline for Member States to transpose the Directive into national law was 31 December 2020.
verbatim_list: the Commission has concluded that these Member States have not yet fully transposed the Directive.
notes: WebFetch 19/10/2026; the 26-state and four-state counts and the 11 October 2025 deadline are from the page body.

title: Transposing the EU's new Product Liability Directive: a Member State progress report
date_evidence: meta-oni_published_date: 2026-09-04T03:18:33; page date September 04, 2026 (updated edition of a June 2026 report)
key_claim: Croatia is the second state after Hungary to complete transposition of the Product Liability Directive; the deadline is 9 December 2026; Belgium, Bulgaria, Estonia, France, Greece, Latvia, Luxembourg, Malta, Slovenia and Spain show no significant progress; divergences may produce forum shopping.
frame_summary: A law firm argues that uneven national transposition of the Product Liability Directive will create inconsistent outcomes across jurisdictions despite its full harmonisation aim.
verbatim_quote: These divergences may give rise to forum shopping and inconsistent outcomes across jurisdictions.
verbatim_list: Member states' transposition deadline is 9 December 2026.
Croatia is now the second state to fully transpose the PLD into national law.
These states are: Belgium, Bulgaria, Estonia, France, Greece, Latvia, Luxembourg, Malta, Slovenia, and Spain.
notes: WebFetch 19/10/2026. Page is an updated version of a June 2026 report; the 4 September 2026 edition is the one cited.

title: EU PTD end of summer round up, 3 September 2026

title: EU Pay Transparency Directive: practical briefing for international employers
date_evidence: 2026年6月30日 (date line of the briefing, Japanese-language page chrome, English text)
key_claim: In late-transposing states public-sector employers face vertical direct effect from 8 June 2026, private employers face directive-consistent interpretation limited by the contra legem principle, and back-pay claims may reach back at least three years.
frame_summary: A law firm argues that employers cannot wait for national law because courts and public bodies already apply the Directive's obligations.
verbatim_quote: Public-sector employers in late-transposing states are subject to vertical direct effect from 8 June 2026.
verbatim_list: Employers should not wait for national implementing legislation.
Back-payment exposure is significant: claims may reach back at least three years.
